results.why: The claim states the same chain: in push-to-stage the external promoter has not moved fresh manifests to the sync branch, so auto-sync applies whatever that branch last held.

The plant attributes the diff failures to the operation running as the narrow destination service account instead of the broad cluster-secret credential, while the claim asserts impersonation never reaches the diff path and that the reporter's belief about the cluster Secret credential is what the design implies.

The claim states the same chain: the reverse deletion strategy waits for each Application to be fully deleted before advancing, so a child stuck Progressing never releases the barrier and the sequence restarts.

The plant's effect is that narrowly scoped destination service accounts silently break server-side diff under fleet-wide impersonation, whereas the claim argues diff stays on the cluster credential and therefore that credential must retain patch authority on every kind, a different route and a different consequence.

The claim states the same chain: one hydrated commit per hydration cycle on the branch the child Applications deploy from, each read as a new source revision by the rolling wave, with no debounce in the design.
